title: The Murder of John Lennon
summary: Hosts Josh and Chuck mark the anniversary of John Lennon's murder outside the Dakota in New York on December 8, 1980. They cover Lennon and Yoko Ono's life in New York, Mark David Chapman's background and mental illness, his stalking of Lennon, the shooting and hospital response, the news breaking on Monday Night Football, the global reaction and vigil, Chapman's psychiatric evaluations, guilty plea, sentencing, parole hearings, and the Strawberry Fields memorial. The episode closes with a listener mail segment from Ben in Utah.
topics: Chapman mental illness and psychiatric evaluations
Monday Night Football Howard Cosell Lennon news
Annie Leibovitz Rolling Stone photo shoot

segments.title: Tour announcement
segments.summary: Hosts promote upcoming live shows in Seattle, Portland, and Sketch Fest in San Francisco in January.

segments.title: Opening and episode framing
segments.summary: Hosts introduce the solemn episode timed near the anniversary of John Lennon's death and mention the related JD Salinger episode.

segments.title: Lennon's New York life
segments.summary: Lennon and Yoko Ono's move from Bank Street after a robbery to the Dakota, its security features, and Lennon's relatively normal life in Manhattan. Discussion of the house-husband era versus reports of depression.

segments.title: Lennon's final years and Double Fantasy
segments.summary: The hosts discuss whether Lennon was depressed or renewed in his final years, including a schooner trip, and the release of Double Fantasy in November 1980.

segments.title: Mark David Chapman's background
segments.summary: Chapman's Fort Worth and Decatur childhood, his abusive father, fantasies as a child, teenage drug use, conversion to Christianity, and early signs of mental illness.

segments.title: Chapman's travels, marriage, and target list
segments.summary: Chapman's move to Hawaii, depression treatment, world trip, marriage to travel agent Gloria Abbe, and a list of famous targets including Lennon. He was a security guard with a gun and traveled to New York in 1980.

segments.title: Break
segments.summary: Ad break before the December 8 narrative.

segments.title: December 8, 1980: the day before the shooting
segments.summary: Lennon and Ono's day, the Annie Leibovitz Rolling Stone photo shoot, an RKO Radio interview, and their departure for the Record Plant. Chapman waited outside the Dakota and met James Taylor the day before, who described Chapman as manic.

segments.title: Autograph and the shooting
segments.summary: Lennon signed Chapman's copy of Double Fantasy outside the Dakota, photographed by Paul Garesh. Later, after Lennon returned just before eleven, Chapman shot him five times, hitting him four times.

segments.title: Immediate aftermath and hospital
segments.summary: Lennon's last words, Chapman waiting calmly with his copy of The Catcher in the Rye, police transport to Roosevelt Hospital, and the pronouncement of death at 11:15.

segments.title: Medical details and news breaks
segments.summary: ER doctor Stephan Glynn's account, autopsy wounds, WABC producer Alan Weiss, and Howard Cosell breaking the news on Monday Night Football during a Patriots-Dolphins game.

segments.title: Global reaction and vigil
segments.summary: Yoko Ono's request for a silent vigil, the ten-minute silence in Central Park, Stevie Wonder's concert announcement, suicides linked to grief, and Paul McCartney's reaction and song Here Today.

segments.title: Beatles and family reaction
segments.summary: Ringo Starr helping with Sean, George Harrison's reaction, Julian Lennon learning the news, and Lennon's cremation at Ferncliff Cemetery.

segments.title: Trial, psychiatric evaluations, and plea
segments.summary: Chapman's court appearance, suicide watch, psychiatric evaluations disputed by prosecution and defense, his guilty plea to second degree murder, and the twenty-to-life sentence at Green Haven.

segments.title: Catcher in the Rye motive and parole
segments.summary: Chapman's identification with Holden Caulfield, his statement reading from the book, the motive to gain fame, and his parole hearings and remorse; Yoko Ono's letters opposing release.

segments.title: Strawberry Fields and Yoko Ono
segments.summary: Strawberry Fields memorial dedicated in 1985, Yoko Ono's continued residence at the Dakota, conspiracy theories blaming her, and the hosts' views on her role in the Beatles breakup.

segments.title: Listener mail from Ben
segments.summary: Hosts read listener mail from thirteen-year-old Ben in Eagle Mountain, Utah, who asks for an episode on epidermolysis bullosa simplex and is named the first to email.
